youtube.description:
Inter's greatest season of all time? Our pick: 1964–65, Helenio Herrera's Grande Inter.
https://www.nerazzurridaily.com/go/yt/?v=debate6 — the Italian Inter press in English every morning, free

THE DEBATE — a weekly fan-made argument, not the news.

1964–65 (Helenio Herrera): Scudetto with 54 points, 22 wins and only 2 defeats in 34 games; European Cup, 1–0 v Benfica at San Siro on May 27, 1965 (Jair); Intercontinental Cup v Independiente, won 1–0 after extra time in the Madrid play-off (Corso). Champions of Italy, Europe and the world in the same season. Coppa Italia runners-up.
2009–10 (José Mourinho): Serie A with 82 points (24 wins, 10 draws, 4 defeats), 2 points ahead of Roma; Coppa Italia, 1–0 v Roma on May 5, 2010 (Milito); Champions League, 2–0 v Bayern Munich in Madrid on May 22, 2010 (Milito ×2). The only treble by an Italian club.
2023–24 (Simone Inzaghi): Serie A with 94 points (29 wins, 7 draws, 2 defeats), 89 scored and 22 conceded, clinched 2–1 in the derby on April 22, 2024 — the 20th title and the second star; Supercoppa Italiana, 1–0 v Napoli on January 22, 2024 (Lautaro Martínez). Out of the Coppa Italia and the Champions League in the round of 16.

Sources: inter.it (club history and honours), uefa.com, Wikipedia (English).
Fan-made — not affiliated with FC Internazionale Milano.

#Inter #ForzaInter #GrandeInter #Treble #SerieA #Shorts

sources.claim: 1964–65 Serie A: Inter 1st, 34 played, 22 W, 10 D, 2 L, 68–29, 54 points; Milan 2nd on 51
1964–65 season page: Herrera; W22 D10 L2; Mazzola 17 league goals; Coppa Italia runners-up; European Cup retained v Benfica
9th Scudetto clinched June 6, 1965 (2–2 v Torino); three trophies: Intercontinental Cup, European Cup (May 27, 1965, 1–0 Benfica), Scudetto
1965 European Cup final: Inter 1–0 Benfica, May 27, 1965, San Siro, Jair (Wikipedia/uefa.com 43', inter.it 42' — minute kept off screen)
uefa.com: Jair 43', Inter the third side to win successive European Cups; Liverpool beaten 4–3 on aggregate in the semi
inter.it finals list: 1965 Inter 1–0 Benfica (Jair); 2010 Bayern 0–2 Inter (Milito 35', 70')
1964 Intercontinental Cup: Independiente 1–0 Inter (Sept 9), Inter 2–0 (Sept 23), play-off Inter 1–0 a.e.t. in Madrid Sept 26, 1964 (Corso 110')
inter.it honours: two Intercontinental Cups under Herrera, 1964 decided by the Madrid play-off (Corso 110') and 1965 v Independiente (3–0, 0–0)
uefa.com on Herrera's Inter 1962–67: European Cups 1964 and 1965, Intercontinental Cups, Scudetti 1962–63, 1964–65, 1965–66
2009–10 Serie A: Inter 38 played, 24 W, 10 D, 4 L, 75–34, 82 points; Roma 80; final day May 16, 2010
2009–10 season page: Mourinho; Serie A, Coppa Italia and Champions League won (2–0 Bayern, May 22, 2010, Milito ×2); Supercoppa lost 2–1 to Lazio; Milito 22 league goals
2010 Coppa Italia final: Inter 1–0 Roma, May 5, 2010, Stadio Olimpico, Milito
2023–24 Serie A: Inter 38 played, 29 W, 7 D, 2 L, 89–22, +67, 94 points; Milan 75; clinched with five games to spare

2023–24 season page: Inzaghi; title clinched April 22, 2024, 2–1 v Milan (Acerbi, Thuram), 20th title/second star; Supercoppa 1–0 Napoli Jan 22, 2024 (Lautaro); Coppa Italia R16 exit v Bologna; CL R16 exit v Atlético on penalties
inter.it recap: 94 points, 89 scored, 22 conceded, best attack and defence, Sommer 19 clean sheets, Lautaro 24 goals, third straight Supercoppa

verification.disputed: Jair's minute in the 1965 final (42' inter.it v 43' Wikipedia/uefa.com) — not shown; 2023–24's 94 points is not the club record (97 in 2006–07) so no 'record' claim is made; the 2010 Club World Cup (Dec 2010) belongs to 2010–11 and is not counted for the treble season
